modules.title: Introduction to Colonial Conquest and Administration
modules.html:
British conquest, indirect rule, and resistance to colonial rule. This section covers introduction to colonial conquest and administration.

Key points

  • The pre-colonial administration of the Bini people was headed by the... — Oba.
  • Which country was the first in Sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence from colonial rule — Ghana.
  • The first capital of colonial Nigeria was _____. — Calabar.
  • The 'Oyo Mesi' were _____ in the pre-colonial Oyo Empire. — king makers.
  • The British 'Policy of Assimilation' was practiced by which colonial power in West Africa — France.

Worked examples

Q: The pre-colonial administration of the Bini people was headed by the...
A: Oba — Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Oba.

Q: Which country was the first in Sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence from colonial rule?
A: Ghana — Under Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana (formerly the Gold Coast) gained independence from Britain in 1957.

quiz.q: The pre-colonial administration of the Bini people was headed by the...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Oba.

quiz.q: Which country was the first in Sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence from colonial rule?
quiz.solution: Under Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana (formerly the Gold Coast) gained independence from Britain in 1957.

quiz.q: The first capital of colonial Nigeria was _____.
quiz.solution: Calabar served as the headquarters of the Oil Rivers Protectorate and the early Southern Nigeria Protectorate.

quiz.q: The 'Oyo Mesi' were _____ in the pre-colonial Oyo Empire.
quiz.solution: They were the hereditary council of seven chiefs responsible for choosing the next Alafin.

quiz.q: The British 'Policy of Assimilation' was practiced by which colonial power in West Africa?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: France.

quiz.q: The colonial policy of Association was by the:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: French.

quiz.q: The primary cause of the collapse of the Old Oyo Empire was _____.
options: the lack of a standing army
internal power struggles and the revolt of Afonja
quiz.solution: Internal friction between the Alafin and the Oyomesi, coupled with the rebellion of Afonja in Ilorin, weakened the empire and led to its fall.

quiz.q: Idris Alooma of Borno is remembered for his military reforms, which included the use of _____.
quiz.solution: Idris Alooma imported firearms and trained musketeers from the Ottoman Empire, giving his army a superior advantage in the 16th century.

quiz.q: The ancient city-state of Kano became the leading commercial center in Hausaland because of its _____.
quiz.solution: Kano was famous for its 'Kano Cloth' and leather works, making it the 'metropolis of the Sudan' in the Trans-Saharan trade.

quiz.q: The principal architect of the Asante Empire was _____.
quiz.solution: Supported by the priest Okomfo Anokye, Osei Tutu unified the Asante clans into a powerful empire.

quiz.q: The Jukun people established their capital at _____.
quiz.solution: Wukari remains the spiritual and traditional headquarters of the Jukun (Kwararafa) kingdom.

quiz.q: King Jaja of Opobo was exiled by the British because he _____.
options: interfered with British palm oil trade in the hinterland
quiz.solution: Jaja insisted on his right to act as a middleman and block British merchants from trading directly with the interior.

quiz.q: The 1914 Amalgamation was primarily funded by revenue from _____.
quiz.solution: The Southern Protectorate was financially self-sufficient, while the North had a deficit; amalgamation allowed the use of Southern funds for Northern administration.

quiz.q: The 1953 'Kano Riot' was triggered by the visit of _____ to the North.
quiz.solution: Action Group leaders visited Kano to campaign for 'Self-government in 1956,' leading to clashes with the NPC supporters.

quiz.q: ECOWAS was established in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: 1975.

quiz.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 introduced:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Regionalism.

quiz.q: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 established:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Federalism.

quiz.q: The discovery of oil in Oloibiri was in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: 1956.

quiz.q: The Kanem-Borno Empire was located near:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Lake Chad.

quiz.q: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Elective principle.

quiz.q: The Ogboni society in Oyo was a:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Secret society/Check on the King.

quiz.q: The Amalgamation of 1914 was by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Lord Lugard.

quiz.q: Ghana Empire was known for:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Gold.

quiz.q: NYSC established by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Gowon.

quiz.q: Samory Toure led:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Mandinka Resistance.

quiz.q: FESTAC 77 held in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Lagos.

quiz.q: Who was the leader of the Action Group (AG)?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Obafemi Awolowo.

quiz.q: The 1963 Constitution replaced the Queen of England with the ___ as Head of State.
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: President.

quiz.q: Badagry is famous for:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Slave trade relics.

quiz.q: Who moved the capital from Lagos to Abuja?
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: Ibrahim Babangida.
